incident.title: Customers charged twice for a single order
incident.alert: Support escalation: 23 tickets in 40 minutes reporting duplicate card charges for one order. Finance reconciliation job flagged 61 orders with more than one captured charge since 18:05 UTC. No error-rate alert fired.

updates.text: Duplicate charges are still happening: 9 more orders were double-charged in the last 5 minutes. Stop the bleeding first, then finish the root cause.

events.text: Investigating duplicate charges (SEV-1) — tracing 61 double-captured orders to their trigger.
Evidence points to blind retries on a non-idempotent charge endpoint timing out at 2s. I'll check runbook guidance before submitting the fix.

args.query: retry non-idempotent POST payment charge timeout idempotency key duplicate

events.label: Searched runbooks "retry non-idempotent POST payment charge" → retries-timeouts-idempotency

evidence.quote: BILL-877: add resilience to gateway calls (retry + circuit breaker)
evidence.supports: A recent change intentionally added retry resilience to gateway calls.
The non-idempotent createCharge POST is annotated for automatic retry; the following lines in this range show POST /v1/charges.
Client read timeout is only 2s, below the gateway's degraded p99 latency.
Retry permits up to three attempts, matching the three charges seen for one order.

evidence.quote: - `POST /v1/charges` creates and captures a charge. It is **not idempotent** by default.
evidence.supports: Repeating the POST can create and capture another distinct charge unless an idempotency key is used.

evidence.quote: - A client-side timeout does not mean the charge failed: the gateway may still complete it.
evidence.supports: A read timeout is ambiguous: the first attempt can succeed server-side while the client retries.

evidence.quote: 18:04 UTC  Degraded performance - Charge API p99 latency elevated (2.5-3.2s). Requests are being processed.
evidence.supports: Trigger: gateway latency rose above the 2s read timeout while requests were still being processed.

evidence.quote: 2026-10-31T18:05:41.112Z  WARN 1 --- [nio-8080-exec-7] i.g.r.retry.internal.RetryImpl : Retry 'paymentGateway', waiting PT0.5S until attempt '2'. Last attempt failed with exception 'java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out'.
evidence.supports: Billing retried the charge after a read timeout at incident start.

evidence.quote: 2026-10-31T18:05:42.903Z charge.succeeded id=ch_3Pq9Wb amount=12999 currency=cad metadata.orderId=ord_90502 created=2026-10-31T18:05:40.981Z
evidence.supports: First webhook shows a distinct successful charge for ord_90502; the next line in range shows a second distinct charge id for the same order and amount.

evidence.quote: 2026-10-31T18:06:11.420Z charge.succeeded id=ch_3PqA0z amount=1950 currency=cad metadata.orderId=ord_90517 created=2026-10-31T18:06:09.877Z
evidence.supports: Ord_90517 received multiple distinct charge.succeeded charges (three lines in this range), matching up to three retry attempts.

evidence.quote: 2026-10-31T18:06:12.851Z  WARN 1 --- [nio-8080-exec-2] i.g.r.retry.internal.RetryImpl : Retry 'paymentGateway', waiting PT0.5S until attempt '3'. Last attempt failed with exception 'java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out'.
evidence.supports: Ord_90517's call reached attempt 3 after repeated read timeouts before finally logging success.

fix.explanation: Remove automatic retry from the non-idempotent POST /v1/charges create operation. Keep the circuit breaker and keep @Retry on the safe GET. This is the smallest reversible change that stops a client read timeout from issuing a second/third charge creation. Do not re-enable create retries until a deterministic Idempotency-Key derived from the order id is sent on every attempt and/or the result is reconciled via GET by orderId before retrying; also review raising the 2s read timeout against gateway latency, but a timeout increase alone is not the fix.

next_steps: Human-approved emergency mitigation: deploy the patch or set paymentGateway retry max-attempts to 1 for createCharge, to stop further duplicate captures while gateway latency is elevated.
Identify and refund/void duplicate captured charges for the 61 flagged orders (and search since 18:05 UTC by metadata.orderId), verifying against gateway records before refunding customers.

Before re-enabling retries on createCharge, add a deterministic Idempotency-Key derived from orderId on every POST /v1/charges attempt, or reconcile with GET /v1/charges?metadata.orderId=... after an ambiguous timeout.
Add alerting on multiple charge.succeeded events for the same metadata.orderId and on retry-after-timeout for payment creation, since eventual retry success suppresses error-rate alerts.
Review read-timeout against gateway p99 latency budget after idempotency is in place.

regression_test.name: createChargeMustNotBeAutomaticallyRetried

report.root_cause: Trigger -> mechanism -> impact: At 18:04 UTC the card gateway's Charge API p99 latency rose to 2.5-3.2s while requests were still being processed, exceeding billing-service's 2s read-timeout. BILL-877 had added Resilience4j @Retry to GatewayClient.createCharge, configured for max-attempts 3 on SocketTimeoutException/IOException. Each attempt issues POST /v1/charges, which is not idempotent by default, and GatewayClient sends no Idempotency-Key. So the first attempt could time out client-side after the gateway had already created/captured the charge; the automatic retry then created a second (and for ord_90517 a third) distinct charge. Retries eventually succeeded, so no error-rate alert fired, but customers were charged multiple times for one order. The ledger 409 for ord_90517 is a downstream consequence of the duplicates, not the cause.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Ledger sync batch-size change (200 -> 500 on 2026-10-31) caused duplicates
ruled_out.reason: Gateway webhooks show distinct charge ids created by the gateway for the same orderId before ledger sync, and the ledger 409 'duplicate external reference ord_90517' follows those duplicate charges; ledger sync is a victim/consequence, not the charge creator.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Duplicate webhook deliveries from the gateway
ruled_out.reason: Webhooks for the same order have different charge ids (e.g. ch_3Pq9Wb vs ch_3Pq9Xk for ord_90502) and different created timestamps/amounts matching separate captures, and finance flagged more than one captured charge.
Billing logs show one capture log per affected order while retry logs and multiple gateway charges occur inside a single call chain/thread (e.g. nio-8080-exec-2 for ord_90517 reaching attempt 3).
Circuit breakers only short-circuit/open; the observed duplication mechanism is explicitly RetryImpl retrying after SocketTimeoutException, up to the configured 3 attempts.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Gateway was failing requests, so retries were safe
ruled_out.reason: Gateway status says requests are being processed despite degraded performance, and docs warn a client timeout does not mean the charge failed; webhooks confirm the timed-out attempts succeeded server-side.

report.summary: Duplicate charges were caused by Resilience4j blindly retrying the non-idempotent POST /v1/charges after 2s read timeouts during gateway latency of 2.5-3.2s, with no Idempotency-Key; remove @Retry from createCharge (keep it on GET) and refund duplicates.

timeline.event: Normal capture before incident: ord_90411 succeeded in 640ms with one charge.
Gateway degraded: Charge API p99 latency elevated to 2.5-3.2s, above billing's 2s read-timeout, while requests were still being processed.
Billing retried paymentGateway to attempt 2 after SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out for ord_90502.
Gateway webhooks show two distinct succeeded charges (ch_3Pq9Wb and ch_3Pq9Xk) for ord_90502, same amount 12999 CAD.
Ord_90517 retried to attempt 3 after read timeouts; webhooks show three distinct succeeded charges for ord_90517.
Ord_90544 retried after a read timeout; webhooks show two distinct succeeded charges for ord_90544.
Ledger sync failed with 409 Conflict duplicate external reference ord_90517, a downstream symptom of duplicate charges.
Ord_90560 succeeded in 1880ms with a single webhook charge and no retry, consistent with latency falling below the timeout for that call.
